title: Effective Quantum Resource Optimization via Circuit Resizing in BQSKit
problem: Quantum circuits in the NISQ era consume significant qubit resources and depth, limiting practical applications on hardware-constrained quantum processors. The challenge is to reduce qubit count while maintaining circuit functionality and ideally improving depth.
motivation: Reducing qubit count enables larger quantum algorithms to run on limited NISQ devices where qubits are expensive and noisy, improving practical utility.
method: The first strategy uses mid-circuit measurements (checking qubit states during computation) and resets to identify unnecessary qubits, then applies gate-dependency rules (analyzing operation order constraints) to remove them—reducing qubit count by 61.6% on average, or 45.3% when also minimizing circuit depth. The second strategy applies numerical instantiation (finding concrete parameter values), synthesis (building operations), and dependency rules to discover resizing opportunities in circuits the first strategy cannot handle, achieving 20.7% average qubit reduction. Both are implemented in BQSKit.
key_novelty: Using mid-circuit measurements and resets combined with gate-dependency analysis makes it possible to shrink quantum circuits that couldn't be reduced before.
contributions: Algorithm 1 achieving 61.6% qubit reduction using gate-dependency rules
Algorithm 2 for previously unresizable circuits with 20.7% average qubit reduction via dependency rules and synthesis
Implementation in BQSKit framework enabling practical circuit optimization
Systematic identification of mid-circuit measurement and reset injection points
